title: The Bystander Effect in Multi-Agent Reasoning: Quantifying Cognitive Loafing in Collaborative Interactions

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the target model's accuracy and sycophantic error adoption when presented with a simulated adversarial consensus from different model brands (e.g., Claude, GPT, Gemini) to quantify intrinsic authority and brand-specific reputational subjugation.

Comparing the target model's cognitive loafing and accuracy when the simulated adversarial swarm consists of its own architectural family (twins) versus out-of-family models (strangers) to measure tribal trust.

Inverting the sequence of auditor models in the prompt to measure the 'Lead Anchor Effect' and primacy weight, demonstrating that the first-listed model in a simulated sequence exerts disproportionate social pressure.
